# Epistle of Barnabas Chapter 1 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET / LOGOS / PNEUMA

---

## Disagreement 1 — v.2: "innate" vs. "naturally endowed" vs. "truly native to you"
- EMET: "so innate is the grace"
- LOGOS: "so naturally endowed is the grace"
- PNEUMA: "something truly native to you"
- **Ruling:** "so naturally endowed is the grace" — *emphytos* means implanted/innate; LOGOS "naturally endowed" is the clearest rendering; EMET's "innate" is acceptable but slightly technical.

## Disagreement 2 — v.4: "long-hoped-for vision of you" vs. "longing for your presence" vs. "how much I have longed to see you"
- EMET: "the long-hoped-for vision of you has struck me"
- LOGOS: "so greatly has the longing for your presence struck me"
- PNEUMA: "How much I have longed to see you! That longing has found its mark"
- **Ruling:** "So greatly has the longing for your presence struck me" — *hoti tosouton epothoun to prosōpon hymōn* — the image is of an intense longing that hits/strikes the writer; LOGOS handles both the force (*tosouton*) and the object (*prosōpon* = face/presence).

## Disagreement 3 — v.7: Three doctrines — "love of joy and gladness" vs. "love that brings joy and gladness"
- EMET: "love of joy and gladness"
- LOGOS: "love of joy and gladness"
- PNEUMA: "love that brings joy and gladness"
- **Ruling:** "love of joy and gladness" — *agapē agalliaseōs kai euphrosynēs* — the genitive is adjectival; retain the literal "love of joy and gladness" as a distinctive phrase.

## Disagreement 4 — v.8: "firstfruits of the taste" vs. "firstfruits of a foretaste"
- EMET: "first-fruits of the taste of things to come"
- LOGOS: "firstfruits of a foretaste of things to come"
- PNEUMA: "foretaste of what is coming"
- **Ruling:** "firstfruits of a foretaste of things to come" — the Greek compounds *aparchēn... proapogeuseōs* — there are two ideas: firstfruits (partial) and pre-tasting (anticipatory); LOGOS retains both; PNEUMA drops "firstfruits."

## Disagreement 5 — v.9: "one of your own" vs. "one of your number"
- EMET: "one of your own"
- LOGOS: "one of your number"
- PNEUMA: "one of your own number"
- **Ruling:** "one of your number" — *heis ex hymōn* literally "one from among you"; all renderings are close; "one of your number" is the most natural English idiom.

**Total disagreements: 5**
